credits: Footage: "NTSB B-Roll - Aerial Imagery of Francis Scott Key Bridge and Cargo Ship Dali", National Transportation Safety Board, 26 March 2024, via Wikimedia Commons (public domain).

frame_0002.jpg.scene: Looking along the remaining approach roadway toward the gap where the main spans were; the ship and collapsed truss beyond.

observations.label: Approach roadway ends abruptly at the collapse
observations.description: The approach road deck stops abruptly where the main spans have fallen. Anyone driving onto the bridge would drive straight into the gap.
observations.visual_evidence: Road deck with lane markings ending in a clean cut over open water.
observations.suggested_fix: Keep road closures at both ends with physical barriers well back from the gap; assess the remaining approach spans and piers.

observations.label: Main truss spans collapsed into the channel
observations.description: The main steel truss spans have collapsed into the water, leaving only a pier and a piece of truss standing beyond the gap.
observations.visual_evidence: Truss sections lying in the water and a single tower of steelwork near the ship.
observations.suggested_fix: Keep the bridge closed and the waterway below restricted; engineers must assess the remaining piers and approach spans before any salvage work starts.

frame_0003.jpg.scene: Directly over the gap: a pier stub and wreckage in the water.

observations.label: Bridge pier destroyed with wreckage in the water
observations.description: A pier that supported the main spans is broken off near water level, with wreckage piled on and around it.
observations.visual_evidence: Broken concrete and steel at water level where a pier stood, debris around it.
observations.suggested_fix: Keep the bridge closed and the waterway below restricted; engineers must assess the remaining piers and approach spans before any salvage work starts.

frame_0004.jpg.scene: Collapsed truss spans lying across the channel toward the ship.

frame_0005.jpg.scene: Remaining pier with a collapsed truss section draped against it.

observations.label: Truss section draped against a damaged pier
observations.description: A large truss section has fallen against this pier and is tangled around it. The pier cap is damaged and the wreckage is unstable.
observations.visual_evidence: Twisted steel truss leaning against a concrete pier column; bent and broken members.
observations.suggested_fix: Keep the bridge closed and the waterway below restricted; engineers must assess the remaining piers and approach spans before any salvage work starts.

frame_0007.jpg.scene: The ship Dali with a collapsed truss span lying across its bow and containers.

observations.label: Truss span lying across the ship's bow
observations.component: collapsed main truss span on the vessel
observations.description: A whole section of the steel truss has fallen across the ship's bow. The ship is pinned under the wreckage and can't be moved until it is cut away.
observations.visual_evidence: Grey truss members spanning the bow, resting on the deck and containers, other truss sections in the water on both sides.
observations.suggested_fix: Stabilise and cut the truss into sections with heavy-lift cranes under an engineered salvage plan before refloating the ship.

observations.label: Containers crushed by falling bridge steel
observations.component: containers on the ship's forward bays
observations.description: Containers at the front of the ship are crushed and knocked over by the falling steel. Some may hold hazardous goods and may be leaking.
observations.visual_evidence: Crumpled and tilted containers under the truss at the bow.
observations.suggested_fix: Check the cargo manifest for dangerous goods in the damaged bays; hazmat teams to inspect and monitor for leaks.

frame_0008.jpg.scene: Top-down view of the bow under the wreckage.

frame_0011.jpg.scene: Collapsed truss spans on both sides of the ship, partly under water.

observations.label: Wreckage blocking the shipping channel
observations.description: Collapsed truss spans lie across the channel on both sides of the ship, closing the shipping channel into the port.
observations.visual_evidence: Truss sections sticking up out of the water across the channel width.
observations.suggested_fix: Keep the channel closed; mark wreckage with buoys; open temporary alternate channels once surveyed; plan wreck removal.

frame_0013.jpg.scene: Wide view: ship, remaining approach span on the right ending in mid-air, truss wreckage in the water.

observations.label: Far-side approach span ends over open water
observations.description: On the far side the approach span also ends over open water.
observations.visual_evidence: Road deck on piers ending at the gap, truss wreckage in the water next to it.
observations.suggested_fix: Keep the far-side closure in place and assess the remaining piers.

frame_0015.jpg.scene: Along the ship's side: bow wreckage and a yellow boom in the water along the hull.

observations.label: Containment boom along the hull (possible fuel release)
observations.description: A yellow containment boom has been laid in the water along the ship's hull, which suggests fuel or oil may be leaking. The sheen itself can't be seen at this distance.
observations.visual_evidence: Continuous yellow floating boom following the hull toward the bow.
observations.extent: Along the length of the hull
observations.suggested_fix: Keep booms in place and monitored; sample the water; check the ship's fuel tanks for damage.

frame_0016.jpg.scene: Close view of the bow under the wreckage with a work boat alongside.

frame_0018.jpg.scene: Open water where the spans were; a pier protection dolphin in the foreground.

summary.summary: NTSB drone footage from 26 March 2024, hours after the container ship Dali struck a main pier of the Francis Scott Key Bridge in Baltimore. The continuous steel truss spans have collapsed into the Patapsco River ({{Main truss spans}}): a main pier is destroyed ({{pier destroyed}}), a truss section is draped against another pier ({{draped}}), and a whole span lies across the ship's bow, pinning it in place ({{across the ship}}). Both approach roadways now end over open water ({{Approach roadway}}, {{Far-side approach}}). Containers at the bow are crushed ({{Containers crushed}}), a containment boom along the hull suggests a possible fuel release ({{Containment boom}}), and the wreckage closes the shipping channel into the Port of Baltimore ({{Wreckage blocking}}). This is a total structural failure; the report's job is to support safe closure, salvage and investigation, not repair.
key_risks: Vehicles or people reaching the open ends of the approach spans ({{Approach roadway}}, {{Far-side approach}}).
Unstable wreckage shifting during salvage onto crews and vessels ({{draped}}, {{across the ship}}).
Hazardous cargo and fuel leaking from damaged containers and the ship ({{Containers crushed}}, {{Containment boom}}).
Port closed until the channel is cleared ({{Wreckage blocking}}).
immediate_actions: Hard road closures with barriers well back from both open ends ({{Approach roadway}}, {{Far-side approach}}).
Marine exclusion zone and wreck marking in the channel ({{Wreckage blocking}}).
Dangerous-goods check of the damaged containers and fuel-leak response ({{Containers crushed}}, {{Containment boom}}).
Preserve evidence for the NTSB investigation.
next_30_days: Engineered salvage plan: cut and lift the truss off the ship and out of the channel ({{across the ship}}, {{Main truss spans}}).
Open temporary alternate channels once surveyed ({{Wreckage blocking}}).
Assess the remaining piers and approach spans for damage ({{pier destroyed}}, {{draped}}).
next_90_days: Demolish or retain the approach spans based on the assessment; design a replacement crossing with pier protection sized for today's ships.
Review pier protection (dolphins/fenders) on other bridges over busy shipping channels.
